look_here_first: Start at the BASE and LEAVES: a tufted perennial with very narrow, inward-rolled (involute) blades. Confirm by viewing the cross section of a fresh, mature leaf. Then examine the often still OPEN but relatively fine/less-showy panicle; do not claim this species has a closed inflorescence. Narrow blades alone are not a species-level diagnosis.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Master Plant Pool Hays-local source. Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center county flora includes Eragrostis lugens. Bell — Hagenbuch & Lemke Hill Country grass treatment cites a Bell County voucher.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: E. lugens has the narrowest, firmest, most involute foliage of this B094 set. E. secundiflora shows clustered spikelets along panicle branches; E. spectabilis forms a much broader airy purple panicle.

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. intermedia and E. spectabilis may form similarly wispy panicles. Narrow, firm, inward-rolled mature leaves and correctly dissected spikelets help separate E. lugens; E. secundiflora has conspicuously crowded, large spikelets, unlike lugens. Similar dropseeds (Sporobolus) differ at individual floret/spikelet architecture; do not use panicle shape alone.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Eragrostis lugens — follow the real-photo field cues
steps: START with the two Harry Rose LIVE tuft photographs: trace fibrous roots upward into ONE leafy crown and emerging tillers, then trace the flowering culms to their complete airy attached panicles. These are source-identified Australian plants, not Texas vouchers.

FIELD CONTEXT: two CC0 North Carolina photographs (soil-rooted leafy tuft + panicle held for detail) came from one source observation. They show where to look on real plants, but iNaturalist still lists it as Needs ID; do not treat their species determination as confirmed or use them for missing ligule proof.

Look at Diego's exact-species leaf/sheath closeup. It shows the narrow blade flexed near a pale collar-like area, but the photo is not proof of the actual tiny 0.2–0.3-mm inner ligule. Obtain a 10–20× peeled-open blade photo with a 1-mm ruler; keep the longer 2–5-mm sheath-throat hairs separate.

At the leaf sheath mouth, keep long hairs DISTINCT from the true very short inner ligule (Harry Rose reports 0.3–0.5 mm, membranous below and hairy above). NO current whole-plant image proves the actual ligule; photograph one peeled-open collar with 1-mm bar.

The pressed Texas voucher images show narrow leaf blades and separate reproductive branches, but flatten natural leaf rolling. Confirm an inrolled blade edge with a fresh cross-section before deciding between similar Eragrostis species.

Record connected roots, young tillers, narrow blade, true ligule and complete attached seedhead from a single Hays-area specimen before strict field-ID completion. Retain existing mature spikelet seed evidence without calling it measured.
The new last same-species panel points only to a physically visible folded blade and adjacent sheathing base, not a proven 0.2–0.3-mm true ligule; do not promote this card to full completion.

Existing two Texas pressed sheets and seed photos remain. Two same-observation NC in-ground/flowerhead context views now in public learner under CC0; iNaturalist quality NEEDS ID so both are strictly provisional species references, no identity or microanatomy arrows. measured_diagnostic_key.evidence_scope: Published GrassBase morphology; measurements not inferred from existing herbarium photos.
measured_diagnostic_key.blades: Mature blades 8–20 cm × 1–2 mm, often involute; verify fresh cross-section.
measured_diagnostic_key.collar: Sheath mouth hairy; ligule fringe of hairs. Photograph with mm scale.
measured_diagnostic_key.panicle: Open, about 18–28 cm long; not necessarily contracted.
measured_diagnostic_key.glumes: Lower about 0.6–1 mm, upper 1.1–1.4 mm; one-veined.
measured_diagnostic_key.lemma: Approximately 1.5–1.6 mm, three-veined; inspect palea keels.
measured_diagnostic_key.awn: Do not infer awn character from pressed vouchers.
measured_diagnostic_key.comparison: E. intermedia, E. spectabilis and E. secundiflora require mature spikelet comparisons; Sporobolus typically has one floret per spikelet.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — FRESH ROLLED BLADES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Narrow, firm perennial leaves about 1–2 mm wide; prove inward rolling on a FRESH blade.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow a live plant from compact perennial tuft to mature narrow blades. Kew GrassBase reports culms about 35–70 cm and blades 8–20 cm × 1–2 mm, often involute. A flattened herbarium sheet or photograph of a bent blade cannot establish naturally inrolled margins. Current live rooted/flowering reference images are source-determined AUSTRALIAN plants, not a Hays County voucher; two North Carolina in-ground views remain identity-provisional.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL HABIT PHOTOS — FRESH BLADE CROSS-SECTION MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · OPEN THE ACTUAL INNER LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Short hair-fringe ligule ~0.2–0.3 mm in Flora Mesoamericana; long sheath-mouth hairs are separate.
field_id_short_tiles.details: At 10–20× peel a mature blade away from its sheath and photograph the INNER ligule with a 1-mm ruler. Kew describes a fringe of hairs but does not supply a length; Flora Mesoamericana reports about 0.2–0.3 mm. Some source-labelled Australian observations describe about 0.3–0.5 mm. Keep this source variation explicit. The existing blade-bend photo exposes outer junction tissue, NOT the true ligule margin; no inner-ligule arrow is justified.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · FOLLOW THE OPEN FLOWERING PANICLE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fine OPEN ovate/pyramidal head about 18–28 cm in Kew; not a contracted seedhead.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew GrassBase reports a panicle about 18–28 × 10–13 cm with slender flexuous branches, often bearded at lower axils. Inspect attached panicle and branch axils on the SAME flowering stem. The Texas pressed specimens and real live Australian flowering photos show an open head; do not teach 'closed panicle' as a defining character. Panicle shape alone overlaps plains and purple lovegrasses.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROSS FLOWERING ARCHITECTURE SHOWN — AXIL SCALE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE THE SMALL MULTIFLORETED SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: Kew spikelets ~3–4.5 mm, usually 5–7 fertile florets; Flora Mesoamericana ~2.4–5 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Use 10–20× and a millimeter scale to isolate several mature laterally compressed spikelets. Kew describes 3–4.5 × 0.5–1 mm and 5–7 fertile florets; Flora Mesoamericana describes 2.4–5 × 0.8–1.3 mm and 3–8 florets. Count florets on one spikelet, not entire flowering branch. Existing USDA caryopsis and Australian seed photographs are useful context but do not establish a local dissected spikelet.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · DISSECT GLUMES, LEMMA AND PALEA
field_id_short_tiles.short: Kew lower glume ~0.6–1 mm; upper ~1.1–1.4 mm; lemma ~1.5–1.6 mm, 3-veined, AWNLESS.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Separate two short one-veined glumes and one mature three-veined fertile lemma under 20–40×. Kew describes an acute lemma tip with no awn and palea keels minutely ciliate. Flora Mesoamericana reports somewhat overlapping glume/lemma ranges (lower ~0.7–1.2 mm, upper ~0.7–1.3 mm, lemma ~1.2–1.6 mm). Do not mark glume vein, palea keel or true awn attachment on an undissected photograph.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES + RELEASE GATE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Distinguish mourning lovegrass from plains and purple lovegrass by FRESH narrow blades plus ripe spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: E. intermedia also has an airy panicle but commonly less rigid, broader blades; E. spectabilis has a more expansive tumbling flowering cloud; E. secundiflora has conspicuous clustered spikelets. Similar Sporobolus often has one floret per spikelet, unlike Eragrostis. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: same-voucher Texas rooted bunch, live involute blade cross-section, peeled inner ligule with scale, lower panicle axil, and glume/lemma dissection. NEEDS_SITE_QA: review eight image records, nine panels, provisional NC identities, Australian source localities, individual CC/NC/public-domain rights, existing arrows and mobile site display. Remain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.
